title: Strait of Hormuz closes
description: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, stops. Pipelines can reroute only part of the flow.

facts.text: About 20 million barrels per day flowed through the strait in 2024, around 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption and over a quarter of seaborne oil trade.
84% of the crude oil and condensate through the strait went to Asia; China, India, Japan and South Korea took a combined 69%.
Saudi and UAE pipelines could bypass about 2.6 million barrels per day.
India imports 88.7% of its crude oil.

affected.note: Largest exporter through the strait: 38% of Hormuz crude (5.5 million b/d).
A top destination for Hormuz crude.
A top destination for Hormuz crude; imports 88.7% of its crude oil.
A top destination for Hormuz crude.
A top destination for Hormuz crude.

title: Bab el-Mandeb shipping halts
description: The Red Sea chokepoint between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, the alternative route for Saudi oil to Asia, is closed to tankers.

facts.text: Houthi forces have seized islands near the strait and struck Saudi oil infrastructure and Red Sea shipping, stepping up pressure on global oil prices.
The strait is a key passage for Saudi oil shipments to Asia and serves as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.
India imports 88.7% of its crude oil.

affected.note: Houthi forces control islands near the strait.
Uses the strait to ship oil to its Asian markets.
An Asian oil importer that depends on imports for 88.7% of its crude.

title: Strait of Malacca is blocked
description: Shipping through the Strait of Malacca, the narrow passage between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea, stops. Ships must detour through Indonesian straits further south.

facts.text: Over 94,000 vessels pass through the strait each year (2008), making it the world's busiest strait and carrying about 25% of the world's traded goods, including oil, Chinese manufactured products, coal and palm oil.
Oil shipments through the strait rose to an estimated 15.2 million barrels per day in 2011.

affected.note: Chinese manufactured exports and oil imports pass through the strait.
Oil from the Middle East reaches East Asia through the strait.
Oil from the Middle East reaches East Asia through the strait.
Borders the strait; ships diverting would use Indonesian straits instead.

title: Suez Canal is closed
description: The Suez Canal, the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe, is blocked. Ships sail around the Cape of Good Hope instead, adding weeks to the journey.

facts.text: The canal was blocked for six days, from 23 to 29 March 2021, by the Ever Given, a container ship that ran aground in it.
The Suez Canal and the SUMED pipeline are a chokepoint for oil moving between the Persian Gulf and Europe.

affected.note: Operates the canal and loses its transit fees while it is closed.
Much of India's trade with Europe uses the canal.
Asia–Europe container traffic uses the canal.
European importers wait longer for goods from Asia.
Mediterranean ports lose the direct route to Asia.

title: Black Sea grain exports halt
description: Grain shipments from Ukraine's Black Sea ports stop, as they did before the 2022 grain deal and after it ended in July 2023.

facts.text: According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, Ukraine provides more than 45 million tonnes of grain a year to the global market.
By mid-July 2023, more than 1,000 shipments under the Black Sea Grain Initiative had carried nearly 33 million tonnes of grain and other food to 45 countries.
The Turkish Straits connect the Black Sea to the Aegean and Mediterranean seas.

affected.note: Its grain exports leave through the Black Sea ports.
A party to the grain deal; its own exports also use the Black Sea.
Controls the straits every Black Sea cargo must pass; brokered the grain deal with the UN.
A large buyer of Black Sea wheat.
Imports wheat from the Black Sea region.

title: Drought cuts Panama Canal traffic
description: Low water levels force the Panama Canal to limit how many ships pass each day, as happened in the 2023 drought.

facts.text: In normal times 36 ships can transit the canal each day; in early December 2023 only 22 a day could, because of low water levels.
Drought and El Niño restrictions pushed up the prices shippers paid for transit slots.

affected.note: US Gulf Coast exports to Asia use the canal.
Receives cargo from the Americas that crosses the canal.
Receives cargo from the Americas that crosses the canal.
West-coast South American trade with the US East Coast uses the canal.

title: Russian seaborne oil is cut off
description: Tighter sanctions stop Russia's seaborne crude exports, going further than the 2022 G7 price cap.

facts.text: A G7 price cap of US$60 per barrel on Russian seaborne crude came into effect on 5 December 2022.

affected.note: Loses its seaborne crude sales.
Became a large buyer of Russian crude after 2022 and would need other suppliers.
A large buyer of Russian crude that would need other suppliers.
Russian Black Sea crude passes the Turkish Straits.

title: OPEC+ makes a deep output cut
description: OPEC+ producers agree to pump much less oil, as in October 2022, tightening world supply.

facts.text: In October 2022, key OPEC+ ministers agreed to cut oil production by 2 million barrels per day, the first cut since 2020.

affected.note: The largest OPEC producer, leading the cut.
Leads the non-OPEC members of OPEC+.
An OPEC member bound by the quotas.
An OPEC member bound by the quotas.
Imports most of its crude, so pays more when supply is cut.

title: Taiwan Strait is blockaded
description: Shipping and air links to Taiwan are cut off, halting exports from the world's largest contract chipmaker.

facts.text: TSMC holds about 70% of the global semiconductor foundry market.
TSMC has grown rapidly with the AI boom because of its importance in making the advanced chips AI needs.

affected.note: Home of TSMC; its chip exports stop.
US tech firms rely on chips made by TSMC.
Its electronics and car industries buy Taiwanese chips.
German carmakers depend on Asian chip supply.
Chinese electronics makers buy chips made in Taiwan.

title: Qatar's LNG exports stop
description: An outage at Ras Laffan, Qatar's gas export hub, halts liquefied natural gas shipments.

facts.text: Ras Laffan Industrial City is Qatar's main site for producing liquefied natural gas, made from gas from the North Field.

affected.note: Its LNG exports leave from Ras Laffan.
A large LNG importer.
A large LNG importer.
Buys LNG from Qatar.
Buys LNG from Qatar.

title: Iran's Kharg oil terminal is knocked out
description: A strike or accident shuts Kharg Island, the terminal that handles most of Iran's oil exports.

facts.text: Kharg Island is the port for up to 90% of Iran's oil exports and stores up to 30 million barrels of oil.

affected.note: Loses most of its oil export capacity.
A buyer of Iranian crude that would need other suppliers.

title: Major hurricane hits the US Gulf Coast
description: A Katrina-strength hurricane shuts offshore platforms and refineries in the Gulf of Mexico.

chokepoint.name: US Gulf of Mexico oil fields

facts.text: Hurricane Katrina (2005) damaged or destroyed 30 oil platforms and closed nine refineries.
Shut-in Gulf of Mexico oil production in the six months after Katrina was about 24% of the year's production, and gas about 18%.

affected.note: Gulf of Mexico oil, gas and refining go offline.
Buys refined fuel from US Gulf Coast refineries.
